Subject: Preemptible tier leasing & burst credits — exploring a hybrid commit

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for taking a look at this. Quick background: NebulaX will be running monthly marketing pushes that drive predictable 6–8 hour spikes (3–5x baseline) plus occasional product launches (12–36 hours, 8–12x). We want to avoid persistent reserved capacity while ensuring we don't have outage risk during the spikes.

Specifically we are interested in:
- A leased preemptible slab we can spin up on short notice for launches
- A bank of "burst credits" that can be consumed against those preemptible GPUs with clear replenishment and eviction rules
- Cost model: prefer a predictable per-month cap rather than per-minute surprises

I've attached a traffic snapshot for Q2 (traffic_snapshot_q2.csv) and can share more peak telemetry if helpful. Can we schedule a 30-min call next week to walk options and get a draft SOW?

Best,
Claire
Claire Han

claire@nebulax.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Preemptible tier leasing & burst credits — exploring a hybrid commit

Claire — thanks for the context and the snapshot. High level proposal below; happy to walk through on a call.

Proposal (summary):
- Lease a preemptible GPU slab (N GPUs of preemptible class; e.g., A10G equivalent) sized to handle typical marketing spike (we recommend 2.5x baseline for monthly pushes, with an optional temporary uplift for launches).
- Burst credits: tokenized credit bank (credits convert to GPU-minutes). Credits consumed first, then preemptible slab used; credits auto-replenish monthly or on a rolling 30-day window.
- Escrow/soft-commit: an optional discounted monthly commit that reduces per-credit cost and guarantees headroom during reserved windows.
- Eviction & fallback: graceful preemption policy (30s KV checkpoint + 90s pre-warm window for hot models) and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants when eviction occurs.

Operational knobs we propose:
- Burst window = configurable per-deal (default 24 hours), credits consumed at peak token/GPU rate.
- Cooldown = 2 hours post-burst to allow KV cache rebuild and to avoid instant re-surge churn.
- Prewarm option: scheduled prewarms for launches (pre-signed job to warm caches 1–4 hours before the window).

Pricing (ballpark):
- Preemptible slab: $X/GPU-hour (discounted for annual commit)
- Burst credits: 1 credit = 1 GPU-minute equivalent; volume tiers reduce per-credit price.
- Cap option: set a monthly cap that prevents charges above agreed threshold; overages require explicit approval.

I've attached an initial pricing brief (preemptible_tier_pricing_v0.2.pdf). Ben / Marissa — tagging you for ops and commercial inputs; would appreciate 1) confirmation on warm-up penalties and 2) whether Finance is comfortable with the capped billing model.

If that looks reasonable, Claire — I can schedule a 30-min scoping call and produce a first-draft SOW with inflight launch support notes and prewarm runbook.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ikhil_sharma@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Preemptible tier leasing & burst credits — proposal and scheduling

Quick ops notes from the infra side:

- GPU types: preemptible A10G-equivalent are best price/perf for short bursts. If NebulaX needs deterministic latency we should propose a mixed slab (small dedicated pool + larger preemptible bank).
- Warm-up: model KV caches take approx 6–12 minutes to reach steady state depending on model size. For high-QPS launches we recommend a staged prewarm (25% -> 50% -> 100% ramp over 60–90 mins) to avoid cold-token spikes.
- Autoscaler knobs: use a dual-trigger autoscaler: 1) latency breach (p90 > target) and 2) token backlog. Add buffer headroom of ~20% during confirmed launches.
- Preemption behavior: we can checkpoint and requeue requests but there is a short tail of failed in-flight requests — we recommend retry/backoff policy in the client and automatic fallback to quantized variants.
- Billing mechanics for credits: credits convert to GPU-minutes at a configurable conversion table (we need to align on conversion factors for mixed GPU types).

I've put together a sample schedule matrix that maps launch phases to prewarm times and credit consumption; see schedule_matrix.xlsx referenced. We should lock a final SLA for eviction tolerance (e.g., 95% of burst requests served without fallback) if they want a hard SLA.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — this looks like a strong approach. Commercial notes:

- We can offer a 15% discount on burst-credit pricing with a 12-month soft-commit (monthly rollback allowed with 60-day notice). The cap option should be firm in the SOW (prevents surprise charges).
- Credit escrow: recommend a rolling escrow account that replenishes on invoice payment to avoid post-burst disputes.
- SLA & exceptions: confirm target p95/p99 latency budgets for the primary endpoints. If NebulaX requires a higher guaranteed success rate during launches we need to size some dedicated reserve (small footprint) to meet it.

Nikhil — please confirm the proposed cap language and whether Finance is comfortable with the escrow flow; I will loop Legal once we have the SOW draft. Claire — happy to be on the call for pricing negotiation.
